measurements.artifact_mechanism: The ~50ms per-response floor is the PROBE DRIVERS' own read-loop park, not product latency. Both the rpc-baseline lane's rpc_probe.py and the rpc-models-persist lane's rpc_probe_gam.py use select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05) inside a 10ms pump window and scan for the response only AFTER the window loop exits: when a response arrives early in the window (fast handler), the loop consumes it, then re-selects with no data pending and PARKS THE FULL 50MS SELECT TIMEOUT before the exit-boundary check runs and the scan finds the frame. The reported wall = product latency (0.1-0.5ms) + one full select park (50.3-50.6ms observed floor). My decompose driver used select(0.01) and measured the identical artifact at 10.2-10.5ms — the floor tracks the select timeout, not the product.
measurements.anomaly_fit: Every per-command anomaly in both prior records fits the park: get_state/get_messages/get_session_stats/set_thinking_level (~50.2-50.6ms) = fast handlers parked; set_auto_compaction 42.0ms/set_follow_up_mode 41.2ms 'below the floor' = the ~40ms fresh-write landed past the 10ms window and was caught ON ARRIVAL; set_session_name 89.9ms = the durable-row write chain (~80ms in the baseline VM's whole-campaign ~40ms fresh-write-rename regime) spanned two windows (park + arrival); new_session 24.8ms and switch_session 82.1ms = assembly exceeding the window, caught on arrival, never parked; get_available_models gam-burst min 10.4ms = the >10ms awaited-refresh handler escaping the window; prompt admission 55.9ms = admission parked. The baseline record's assertion '~40-50ms is real surface latency, not quantization' is corrected: it IS quantization (the select park), the third driver-side measurement artifact disclosed on this surface.
